chess-salesforce.prompt: Build a chess rules engine in Apex with a simple Lightning web component board, in a Salesforce DX project in the current directory, and deploy and test it in the Salesforce Developer Edition org with alias `de`. Use `--target-org de` on every `sf` command that talks to the org; the CLI is already logged in, so never ask for, print or store credentials, and never run `sf org display` (it prints an access token). Name every Apex class `SLChess...` (for example `SLChessEngine`) and the component `slChessBoard`. Besides the Apex classes and the component, create exactly these kinds of metadata, all named with the prefix `SLChess`, so that the board opens in the org and the work can still be removed afterwards: a custom tab `tabs/SLChess_Board.tab-meta.xml` that is a Lightning component tab (`<lwcComponent>slChessBoard</lwcComponent>`; the component's meta file exposes the `lightning__Tab` target), a Lightning app `applications/SLChess.app-meta.xml` (standard navigation, containing that tab) and, if you want one, a Lightning app page `flexipages/SLChess_<Name>.flexipage-meta.xml` (then the component's meta file also exposes `lightning__AppPage`). Create no other metadata (no custom objects, fields, permission sets, static resources, triggers, profiles, labels or flows), and do not change profiles or permission sets. The Salesforce DX project root (`sfdx-project.json` and `force-app/`) is the current directory itself, not a subfolder. `SLChessEngine` is a public class with static methods only; a position is a FEN string. `startFen()` returns the standard start position. `legalMoves(String fen)` returns a `List<String>` of every legal move for the side to move in UCI form (for example `e2e4`, and `e7e8q` for a promotion), sorted alphabetically. `applyMove(String fen, String move)` returns the FEN after the move, with correct castling rights, en-passant square, halfmove clock and fullmove number, or throws `SLChessEngine.IllegalMoveException` (a public exception class you define inside `SLChessEngine`) when the move is not legal. The en-passant target square is set after every two-square pawn push, whether or not a capture is possible (the FEN-spec convention). `status(String fen)` returns `ongoing`, `check`, `checkmate` or `stalemate` for the side to move. Extend the server's user listing, GET /users, with filtering and pagination. The `name` query parameter keeps only the users whose name contains it as plain text, ignoring case; an empty `name` keeps every user. The `page` and `size` query parameters ask for one page of those users in id order, page 1 holding the first `size` of them. When either is given, the answer is a JSON object with "page", "size", "total" (how many users matched), "pages" (how many pages they fill, 0 when none matched) and "items" (the users on that page); `size` is 10 when only `page` is given and `page` is 1 when only `size` is given, and a page after the last one answers an empty "items". `page` must be a whole number of at least 1 and `size` a whole number from 1 to 100: any other value, an empty one included, answers HTTP 400 with a JSON object whose "error" says what is wrong. Keep the API compatible: without `page` and `size`, GET /users still answers a JSON array of users in id order (every user unless `name` is given), any other query parameter is ignored, and GET /users/:id is unchanged. Everything the project already does keeps working, and its existing tests must still pass as they are. Add node:test tests under test/ for the new behaviour; `npm test` runs them with the existing ones.

ticket-escalation.prompt: Extend the ticket service with bulk reassignment and escalation. `POST /tickets/reassign` with `{"from": "<agent>", "to": "<agent>"}` moves every open or in-progress ticket assigned to `from` over to `to` and answers `{"moved": <how many>, "ids": [<their ids in id order>]}`; `from` and `to` must be two different agents. Each moved ticket's new agent is notified as for a single assignment. grok-chat-salesforce.prompt:
Use ShipLoop to build and deliver a Grokbot-style chat application inside Salesforce, with its agent harness implemented directly in Apex and a usable Lightning web component UI. The purpose is to exercise ShipLoop's complete prepare, implement, test, evaluate, repair and rerun workflow on a realistic Salesforce application. Design and build the application in this run; no application implementation is supplied. Emulate conversational work with tools, visible progress and approval of record changes. A desktop computer, shell, general web browser or unrestricted autonomous agent is outside the product scope.

Environment and delivery contract
You are working in a Salesforce org environment, not just building a local web mockup. The Salesforce DX project root (sfdx-project.json and force-app/) is this directory. The target is the existing Developer Edition org with alias de; pin every org-facing sf command with --target-org de. The CLI is already authenticated, but that does not prove the browser or the model provider is configured. Do not print or store credentials or run sf org display. Use the provided guarded sf command and respect its refusals; do not bypass it with another executable, raw API or alternate org. All app construction belongs in the delivered repository.

Use SLGrokChat as the Apex and metadata prefix and slGrokChat as the LWC prefix. Expose the app through SLGrokChatController with AuraEnabled methods, the slGrokChatApp component with lightning__Tab, the SLGrokChat_Chat Lightning component tab and the SLGrokChat Lightning app containing that tab. Keep source under force-app/main/default. Supporting Apex classes and LWC bundles may use the same prefixes. Apex test class names end in Test. Create SLGrokChatItem__c for synthetic business records. You may also create SLGrokChatThread__c, SLGrokChatMessage__c, SLGrokChatAction__c and SLGrokChatConfig__c for conversation, message, pending-action and non-secret setup state. No other custom objects, custom settings, custom metadata types or platform events are allowed. Do not schedule background jobs. The only permitted object relationships point from an owned child to SLGrokChatThread__c; Thread has no relationships. This keeps the shared cleanup order child-before-parent. Use private sharing for independent objects and controlled-by-parent sharing only for children of owned objects. Do not add relationships to foreign objects. Use exactly one permission set, SLGrokChat_Access, granting only necessary app/class access and read/create/edit access to each delivered owned object except Config, and to the work-item Status__c/Notes__c fields. Any Config grant is read-only, with no editable Config fields; administrator-only configuration writes rely on separately held administrator authority. Grant other delivered fields only as needed; no delete, view-all, modify-all or system permissions. Assign it only to the current CLI user. Create no profiles, triggers, flows, static resources, Named Credentials, External Credentials or other metadata. Never change existing or foreign metadata or records. This is a fresh-prefix case with default harness cleanup; do not use --keep-platform. Cleanup covers tracked owned state, not arbitrary effects elsewhere in the org.

The assistant and its runtime prompt
Provide an Apex-owned conversation and tool-execution loop that calls a supported Grok API using the owner-configured Named Credential Grok_Chat_Model and the documented xAI Responses API function-calling protocol. Record the documentation/API version used. Keep the credential reference/model choice in non-secret, server-enforced administrator-only configuration and document the supported API and tool-call format actually used. The browser must not hold a provider key or call the provider directly. Preserve conversations, tool results and action status across a page reload, separated by Salesforce user; allow a new conversation without destroying earlier history. Display pending work, actual results, recoverable failures and cancellation clearly in a keyboard-accessible Lightning UI. Do not present a delayed or failed operation as completed.

Author and retain the actual runtime system prompt in the application source. It must explicitly tell the model that it operates inside this Salesforce org on behalf of the current user. Allow fixed, non-secret org/current-user identity reads in addition to the scoped business tools. Supply authoritative org identity, current-user context, permitted object/field scope and available tool schemas from the server; never take an org identity or permission claim from chat text as authority. Instruct the model to use real structured tool calls to inspect schema, find/read allowed records and propose create/update operations. Execute validated calls in Apex and return their real results to the model before it describes the outcome. Natural-language promises, invented records and merely printing a tool-call JSON example do not count as tool use. Distinguish the builder's sf tooling from the tools exposed to users of the finished assistant. Treat record contents, tool output and user/model text as data that cannot expand privileges or alter the tool registry.

Read and modify Salesforce records in v1
Include a small synthetic work-item object SLGrokChatItem__c with a text Name, Status__c restricted to Open or Done, and Notes__c text. The assistant's business tools may find/read these records and propose their creation or updates to those three fields. Other owned objects store internal conversation/setup/action state and are not exposed as arbitrary business-edit tools. The app may seed clearly labeled synthetic work items through an explicit UI action. Never use production/customer records as fixtures. Internal conversation bookkeeping may persist automatically; business record creation and changes always require the user's confirmation.

Show a specific proposed operation, target record (or new record), and old/new field values before allowing confirmation. Enforce authorization in Apex independently of the runtime prompt: sharing, object and field permissions, allowed object/field names, argument types and record ownership/access are checked at execution. Confirmation must bind to that user, org and exact proposal. Changed arguments or stale record values require a new proposal and confirmation. A cancel, refusal, expired approval, duplicate click, retry, page reload or replay must not cause an extra or broader write. The model cannot approve its own proposal. Execute only validated registry tools; never accept arbitrary SOQL, dynamic Apex, Execute Anonymous, shell/code execution, metadata changes or broad exports as tool arguments. Fixed, scoped queries inside implemented read tools are expected. Report structured errors for unknown tools, malformed arguments, unauthorized or missing records and failed writes. A failed action must leave a truthful durable status; retries must not duplicate successful writes.

Setup detection and guided setup
On first access, deterministically check local configuration and the current user's access before requiring any successful model call. If setup is incomplete, display a usable setup walkthrough instead of a broken chat screen. Missing model configuration is a product scenario to handle, not a reason to skip building or testing the setup experience. Explain which non-secret setting is missing, who can supply it, and the next concrete action. Guide an authorized administrator through configuring the supported modern Named Credential/External Credential and principal access in Salesforce Setup using an administrator-owned permission set outside the SLGrokChat prefix, then let the user select/reference that existing configuration and model and test the connection. Do not create or modify credentials in this run, ask for API keys/passwords in chat, or put secrets in source, logs, screenshots or evidence. If administrator input is required, name that exact remaining step while continuing independent implementation and offline tests.

Setup must work before the provider is available. Rechecking and page reload within a run must preserve valid app configuration and conversations. Harness cleanup between runs removes prefix-owned app state; owner-managed credentials remain outside its tracked coverage and must not be changed. Do not claim their preservation was independently verified. Distinguish confirmed missing configuration, missing user/principal access, provider authentication failure, provider outage/rate limiting and an unknown diagnosis. Do not infer a missing credential or expose secret values from a generic callout failure. A configured app should enter chat without repeating onboarding. Include a safe way to revisit setup and recover after configuration is corrected. Handle Salesforce callout/transaction constraints and provider errors explicitly, without silently replacing a failed live call with mock output.

Evaluation journeys
1. With no provider reference, open the real deployed app and complete the visible steps that do not require an administrator or provider; verify useful setup status, no attempted chat-as-setup dependency and no business-record write. Recheck and reload without losing progress. With valid configuration, verify the setup test and transition into chat. Exercise inaccessible/invalid configuration separately from an unavailable provider. If a live credential is unavailable, retain those live-dependent results as UNKNOWN and explain the exact setup step still required.
2. Ask the assistant what org and user it is working for, then ask it to find/read a known synthetic work item. Observe a real tool invocation and compare the result with Salesforce data. A chat answer by itself is not proof of an org read.
3. Request a new work item and an update to an existing one. Inspect each proposal and confirm it in the UI; independently query the org to verify the exact persisted values. Cancel a separate proposal and verify no write. Try stale data, edited arguments, duplicate confirmation/retry and replay; verify refusal or the same already-recorded outcome, without a second mutation. Verify permission-denied and cross-user authority paths with isolated System.runAs tests; an administrator browser session alone is insufficient proof. If a second authorized browser identity is available, separately verify that one user's conversation or confirmation is not another user's authority.
4. Inject a malformed/unknown tool call, unauthorized field/object request and instructions embedded in a record. Verify validation and useful errors without expanded access. Exercise provider authentication failure, rate limiting/unavailability and a failed write; show recoverable state and preserve the conversation. Unit mocks can exercise deterministic errors, but label them as mocks and keep them distinct from real-provider results.
5. Reload the app, reopen the conversation and inspect its tool/action history. Verify a usable layout, focus/keyboard access, loading/error states and safe text rendering. Attempt to access the UI first using discovered testing tools; prefer an already available Chrome DevTools route. Verify the browser target is the declared org before interacting with it. Only if access requires authentication, find the minimal authorized route using the existing browser session, harness-supported sf authentication handoff, or an available approved credential service such as 1Password. Do not install an integration or bypass a guard to obtain access. Retain an exact blocker if no supported route is available. Authentication/setup success, rendered UI success and correct persisted behavior are separate evidence.

Code, comments and tests
Implement meaningful Apex tests using HttpCalloutMock and isolated test data, plus useful UI/local checks where supported. Cover successful tool round trips and confirmed writes as well as the negative cases above. Run target-native tests in the org; at least eight Apex test methods across prefix-owned Test classes are required as a smoke floor, not proof of coverage. Keep all documented test helpers inside the delivered repository so a fresh checkout can run them. Include setup, deployment, test and recovery instructions and preserve the runtime prompt for review.

During evaluation, explicitly review code quality, sufficient input/error checking, and comment/annotation quality. Put concise explanations beside non-obvious invariants: the authority boundary, confirmation binding/replay handling, transaction/callout ordering, persistence ownership and recovery semantics. Comments should preserve reasons and constraints, not narrate obvious code or make unverified claims. When a rejected approach or removed behavior creates a real recurrence risk, leave an appropriate tombstone explaining what must not return and why, with an evidence/test reference; do not manufacture tombstones or a comment quota. Evaluate whether those annotations are accurate and sufficient. Record actionable findings with code locations, fix them and rerun the relevant tests, retaining failures and rerun evidence.

Finish with a committed, reproducible delivery and an evidence-based acceptance report for every journey. Separate source/deployment smoke checks, builder-authored unit tests, independent org observations, rendered UI evidence, live Grok responses and code/comment review. The initial case's automated checks cover project scope/layout, deployed artifacts and the Apex test run only; they do not independently prove live chat, setup usability, confirmation authorization or UI behavior. Never turn an unobserved result into PASS or call partial smoke coverage full E2E success. Record exact remaining blockers/UNKNOWNs and use the observed defects to guide the next ShipLoop improvement-and-rerun round.

This is an exploratory first-run case. Its final acceptance check deliberately returns UNKNOWN until an independent behavioral oracle is calibrated; do not edit the harness or repeatedly repair a working app to bypass that placeholder. Complete independent work, report setup/access blockers and hand off the evidence without waiting indefinitely for a human. A blocked live-provider step does not excuse missing source, deployment or offline tests. The case cannot yet produce a qualified full-E2E PASS.

gym-membership-salesforce.prompt:
Use ShipLoop to build and deliver an internal gym membership application in a Salesforce DX project rooted in the current directory, deploying to the already-authenticated Developer Edition org alias de. This is a fresh development task: implement the application yourself through ShipLoop. Every org-talking sf command must specify --target-org de. Never request, print or store credentials; do not run sf org display or sf org open. The provided gym-ui command handles its own fresh authenticated browser. Keep all changes within the reserved SLGym/slGym namespace and the owned objects below; preserve other applications and records. Use API version 60.0 and no external integrations, payments, public portals, persistent users, jobs, flows, triggers, profiles or extra permission sets.

Build four usable journeys: member self-service, administrative membership management, member 360, and a coaching check-in kiosk. The product is small: membership/profile plus visit history. Create exactly two custom objects, SLGymMember__c and SLGymVisit__c. Both use an AutoNumber Name. SLGymMember__c has Private sharing and fields LoginUserId__c (unique nullable Text18), FullName__c (Text80), Email__c (Email), Goal__c (Text80), Plan__c (restricted picklist Basic/Coached), Status__c (restricted picklist Active/Frozen/Cancelled). SLGymVisit__c has ControlledByParent sharing, Member__c (MasterDetail to SLGymMember__c only), CheckedInAt__c (DateTime), Coaching__c (TextArea). Do not mark other fields required at metadata level: validate required values in the controller. Add no fields on other objects. All sample/test addresses and usernames end in @example.invalid.

Expose @AuraEnabled public static methods on SLGymController, returning JSON Strings with this contract. Successful single-member methods return the member DTO; listMembers returns a DTO array and absent getMyMembership returns the JSON string null. A member DTO contains id, fullName, email, goal, plan, status, loginUserId, visitCount, coaching (latest stored coaching, null/empty with no visits). getMyMembership() returns that DTO or the JSON string "null". saveMyMembership(String fullName,String email,String goal,String plan) creates or edits only the caller's own linked member, binding LoginUserId__c to UserInfo.getUserId(); first enrollment is Active, and later profile/plan edits preserve the status, including Frozen or Cancelled. setMyStatus(String status) supports Active/Frozen for the caller's own membership, but refuses any self-service status change from Cancelled, even when the caller is an admin. adminSave(String memberId,String fullName,String email,String goal,String plan,String status) is admin-only; a null/empty memberId creates an unlinked member and an update preserves the existing LoginUserId__c. listMembers() is an admin-only DTO array. member360(String memberId) is restricted to that linked member or an admin and includes the persisted visit count and latest stored coaching. checkIn(String memberId) has the same ownership rule and returns the member DTO plus visitId. Identify admin authority server-side using the current user's Profile.PermissionsModifyAllData; never trust a client role flag. Declare sharing explicitly and enforce CRUD/FLS as well as logical authorization (user-mode operations or equivalent).

The state/action rules are: profile save preserves Active, Frozen or Cancelled; self freeze/resume supports Active/Frozen and refuses Cancelled; admin may set any of the three statuses; check-in checks status FIRST and only Active is eligible. Repeated sequential check-in on the same Date.today() in the running user's time zone returns the same persisted visitId without another visit. After freezing/cancelling an already checked-in member, another check-in still refuses. This is sequential idempotency; no concurrent-call guarantee is requested. A later calendar day creates a new visit. Basic coaching contains "independent training" case-insensitively; Coached coaching contains the saved goal case-insensitively. History reports stored coaching, not recomputed text after a profile change; latest visit is ordered by CheckedInAt__c then Id. Invalid/foreign/missing IDs, plans, statuses or required fullName/email/goal refuse. Refusal means AuraHandledException (Aura ERROR) with no persisted state change, not SUCCESS with an error payload. Full names and goals must be nonblank and within field length; use syntactically valid email addresses.

Build slGymApp as the LWC exposed to lightning__Tab; SLGym_Members is its Lightning component tab, SLGym is its standard-navigation Lightning app containing that tab. SLGym_Access is the only permission set: grants app visibility, Visible tab access and controller/class access; read/create/edit on the two objects, delete=false, viewAllRecords=false and modifyAllRecords=false. Grant read/edit FLS for every nonrequired custom field; omit fieldPermissions for the inherent required MasterDetail Member__c. Add no userPermissions. After deploy, assign it only to the current existing CLI user with sf org assign permset --name SLGym_Access --target-org de. Apex classes must start SLGym and test class names must end in Test (SLGym...Test); no SLGymOracleTest product class (independent verification uses that name in a check-only validation after your session). No extra metadata types or schema. The guarded CLI refuses interactive schema generation; write the declared metadata files directly.

Use these stable accessible labels so a person and independent checker can exercise the same app. Self-service inputs/comboboxes: My full name, My email, My goal, My plan. Buttons: Save my membership, Freeze my membership, Resume my membership. Show visible My status: <status>. Admin inputs: Admin full name, Admin email, Admin goal, Admin plan, Admin status. Buttons: Create member and Save member. Member list buttons: Manage member <fullName> (loads admin form) and View member <fullName> (opens 360). The selected 360 shows Selected member: <name>, Selected email: <email>, Selected goal: <goal>, Selected plan: <plan>, Selected status: <status>, Visit count: <n>. The kiosk has Check in selected member and visible Coaching: <text>. Keep that button enabled to exercise server refusals; a refused check-in visibly says Check-in refused. Native selects or lightning-combobox are both acceptable. Render saved controller results and refresh them after mutations/reload. The existing org user is an admin who can also enroll as a member; self-service rules still apply to that identity. Do not provision another browser user.

Deploy, assign access and run your Apex tests in the org, at least eight passing methods with isolated data and no SeeAllData. Cover self binding, member/admin authorization, validation, profile edits while frozen/cancelled, status-before-dedup, active/repeated/yesterday check-in and both coaching plans. Test-created users may be used only inside isolated Apex tests, not as permanent accounts. Run each test class synchronously with sf apex run test --target-org de --class-names <Class> --synchronous --result-format human --code-coverage. Before declaring completion, run the supplied gym-ui command and fix any failures it reports. It independently exercises self/admin/360/kiosk in a fresh browser, correlates controller mutations with UI results, reloads, and checks persisted records. It uses fresh synthetic admin-created members for check-ins so repeated builder/final checks do not collide. Do not stop until Apex and gym-ui pass. Document how to deploy and use the app.

shared-expenses.prompt: Build a small shared-expenses service in Node.js (no npm dependencies). server.js listens on the port in the PORT environment variable and keeps its data in the JSON file named by the DATA_FILE environment variable, so groups and expenses survive a restart. POST /groups with {"id": "<group id>", "members": ["<name>", ...]} creates a group: 201, 409 if the id exists, and 400 unless members holds at least two distinct non-empty names. POST /groups/<id>/expenses records an expense paid by one member. {"payer": "<name>", "cents": <positive integer>, "split": "equal"} shares it equally among all members, with any cents left over after an even division going one each to the members listed first. {"payer": "<name>", "cents": <positive integer>, "split": "exact", "shares": {"<name>": <cents>, ...}} makes each member listed in shares owe that many whole cents (zero is allowed), and the shares must add up to cents. It answers 201 with {"expense": <n>}, where n is 1 for the group's first expense, then 2, and so on; 400 for an unknown payer or member, a non-positive or non-integer amount, an unknown split, or shares that do not add up. GET /groups/<id>/balances returns an object with each member's net cents, what they paid minus what they owe, so the balances add up to 0. GET /groups/<id>/settlements returns a JSON array of {"from", "to", "cents"} payments that bring every balance to 0: repeatedly the member who owes most pays the member who is owed most the smaller of the two amounts, and ties go to the member listed first. Every route under /groups/<id> answers 404 for an unknown group. Concurrent requests must never lose an expense. Cover the behaviour with node:test tests under test/ that run with `node --test`.

grok-chat-salesforce-full.prompt:
Use ShipLoop to build and deliver a Grokbot-style chat application inside Salesforce, with its agent harness implemented directly in Apex and a usable Lightning web component UI. The purpose is to exercise ShipLoop's complete prepare, implement, test, evaluate, repair and rerun workflow on a realistic Salesforce application. Design and build the application in this run; no application implementation is supplied. Emulate conversational work with tools, visible progress and approval of record changes. A desktop computer, shell, general web browser or unrestricted autonomous agent is outside the product scope.

Environment and delivery contract
You are working in a Salesforce org environment, not just building a local web mockup. The Salesforce DX project root (sfdx-project.json and force-app/) is this directory. The target is the existing Developer Edition org with alias de; pin every org-facing sf command with --target-org de. The CLI is already authenticated, but that does not prove the browser or the model provider is configured. Do not print or store credentials or run sf org display. Use the provided guarded sf command and respect its refusals; do not bypass it with another executable, raw API or alternate org. All app construction belongs in the delivered repository.

Use SLGrokChat as the Apex and metadata prefix and slGrokChat as the LWC prefix. Expose the app through SLGrokChatController with AuraEnabled methods, the slGrokChatApp component with lightning__Tab, the SLGrokChat_Chat Lightning component tab and the SLGrokChat Lightning app containing that tab. Keep source under force-app/main/default. Supporting Apex classes and LWC bundles may use the same prefixes. Apex test class names end in Test. Create SLGrokChatItem__c for synthetic business records. You may also create SLGrokChatThread__c, SLGrokChatMessage__c, SLGrokChatAction__c and SLGrokChatConfig__c for conversation, message, pending-action and non-secret setup state. No other custom objects, custom settings, custom metadata types or platform events are allowed. Do not schedule background jobs. The only permitted object relationships point from an owned child to SLGrokChatThread__c; Thread has no relationships. This keeps the shared cleanup order child-before-parent. Use private sharing for independent objects and controlled-by-parent sharing only for children of owned objects. Do not add relationships to foreign objects. Use exactly one permission set, SLGrokChat_Access, granting only necessary app/class access and read/create/edit access to each delivered owned object except Config, and to the work-item Status__c/Notes__c fields. Any Config grant is read-only, with no editable Config fields; administrator-only configuration writes rely on separately held administrator authority. Grant other delivered fields only as needed; no delete, view-all, modify-all or system permissions. Assign it only to the current CLI user. Create no profiles, triggers, flows, static resources, Named Credentials, External Credentials or other metadata. Never change existing or foreign metadata or records. This is a fresh-prefix case with default harness cleanup; do not use --keep-platform. Cleanup covers tracked owned state, not arbitrary effects elsewhere in the org.

The assistant and its runtime prompt
Provide an Apex-owned conversation and tool-execution loop that calls a supported Grok API using the owner-configured Named Credential Grok_Chat_Model and the documented xAI Responses API function-calling protocol. Record the documentation/API version used. Keep the credential reference/model choice in non-secret, server-enforced administrator-only configuration and document the supported API and tool-call format actually used. The browser must not hold a provider key or call the provider directly. Preserve conversations, tool results and action status across a page reload, separated by Salesforce user; allow a new conversation without destroying earlier history. Display pending work, actual results, recoverable failures and cancellation clearly in a keyboard-accessible Lightning UI. Do not present a delayed or failed operation as completed.

Author and retain the actual runtime system prompt in the application source. It must explicitly tell the model that it operates inside this Salesforce org on behalf of the current user. Allow fixed, non-secret org/current-user identity reads in addition to the scoped business tools. Supply authoritative org identity, current-user context, permitted object/field scope and available tool schemas from the server; never take an org identity or permission claim from chat text as authority. Instruct the model to use real structured tool calls to inspect schema, find/read allowed records and propose create/update operations. Execute validated calls in Apex and return their real results to the model before it describes the outcome. Natural-language promises, invented records and merely printing a tool-call JSON example do not count as tool use. Distinguish the builder's sf tooling from the tools exposed to users of the finished assistant. Treat record contents, tool output and user/model text as data that cannot expand privileges or alter the tool registry.

Read and modify Salesforce records in v1
Include a small synthetic work-item object SLGrokChatItem__c with a text Name, Status__c restricted to Open or Done, and Notes__c text. The assistant's business tools may find/read these records and propose their creation or updates to those three fields. Other owned objects store internal conversation/setup/action state and are not exposed as arbitrary business-edit tools. The app may seed clearly labeled synthetic work items through an explicit UI action. Never use production/customer records as fixtures. Internal conversation bookkeeping may persist automatically; business record creation and changes always require the user's confirmation.

Show a specific proposed operation, target record (or new record), and old/new field values before allowing confirmation. Enforce authorization in Apex independently of the runtime prompt: sharing, object and field permissions, allowed object/field names, argument types and record ownership/access are checked at execution. Confirmation must bind to that user, org and exact proposal. Changed arguments or stale record values require a new proposal and confirmation. A cancel, refusal, expired approval, duplicate click, retry, page reload or replay must not cause an extra or broader write. The model cannot approve its own proposal. Execute only validated registry tools; never accept arbitrary SOQL, dynamic Apex, Execute Anonymous, shell/code execution, metadata changes or broad exports as tool arguments. Fixed, scoped queries inside implemented read tools are expected. Report structured errors for unknown tools, malformed arguments, unauthorized or missing records and failed writes. A failed action must leave a truthful durable status; retries must not duplicate successful writes.

Setup detection and guided setup
On first access, deterministically check local configuration and the current user's access before requiring any successful model call. If setup is incomplete, display a usable setup walkthrough instead of a broken chat screen. Missing model configuration is a product scenario to handle, not a reason to skip building or testing the setup experience. Explain which non-secret setting is missing, who can supply it, and the next concrete action. Guide an authorized administrator through configuring the supported modern Named Credential/External Credential and principal access in Salesforce Setup using an administrator-owned permission set outside the SLGrokChat prefix, then let the user select/reference that existing configuration and model and test the connection. Do not create or modify credentials in this run, ask for API keys/passwords in chat, or put secrets in source, logs, screenshots or evidence. If administrator input is required, name that exact remaining step while continuing independent implementation and offline tests.

Setup must work before the provider is available. Rechecking and page reload within a run must preserve valid app configuration and conversations. Harness cleanup between runs removes prefix-owned app state; owner-managed credentials remain outside its tracked coverage and must not be changed. Do not claim their preservation was independently verified. Distinguish confirmed missing configuration, missing user/principal access, provider authentication failure, provider outage/rate limiting and an unknown diagnosis. Do not infer a missing credential or expose secret values from a generic callout failure. A configured app should enter chat without repeating onboarding. Include a safe way to revisit setup and recover after configuration is corrected. Handle Salesforce callout/transaction constraints and provider errors explicitly, without silently replacing a failed live call with mock output.

Evaluation journeys
1. With no provider reference, open the real deployed app and complete the visible steps that do not require an administrator or provider; verify useful setup status, no attempted chat-as-setup dependency and no business-record write. Recheck and reload without losing progress. With valid configuration, verify the setup test and transition into chat. Exercise inaccessible/invalid configuration separately from an unavailable provider. If a live credential is unavailable, retain those live-dependent results as UNKNOWN and explain the exact setup step still required.
2. Ask the assistant what org and user it is working for, then ask it to find/read a known synthetic work item. Observe a real tool invocation and compare the result with Salesforce data. A chat answer by itself is not proof of an org read.
3. Request a new work item and an update to an existing one. Inspect each proposal and confirm it in the UI; independently query the org to verify the exact persisted values. Cancel a separate proposal and verify no write. Try stale data, edited arguments, duplicate confirmation/retry and replay; verify refusal or the same already-recorded outcome, without a second mutation. Verify permission-denied and cross-user authority paths with isolated System.runAs tests; an administrator browser session alone is insufficient proof. If a second authorized browser identity is available, separately verify that one user's conversation or confirmation is not another user's authority.
4. Inject a malformed/unknown tool call, unauthorized field/object request and instructions embedded in a record. Verify validation and useful errors without expanded access. Exercise provider authentication failure, rate limiting/unavailability and a failed write; show recoverable state and preserve the conversation. Unit mocks can exercise deterministic errors, but label them as mocks and keep them distinct from real-provider results.
5. Reload the app, reopen the conversation and inspect its tool/action history. Verify a usable layout, focus/keyboard access, loading/error states and safe text rendering. Attempt to access the UI first using discovered testing tools; prefer an already available Chrome DevTools route. Verify the browser target is the declared org before interacting with it. Only if access requires authentication, find the minimal authorized route using the existing browser session, harness-supported sf authentication handoff, or an available approved credential service such as 1Password. Do not install an integration or bypass a guard to obtain access. Retain an exact blocker if no supported route is available. Authentication/setup success, rendered UI success and correct persisted behavior are separate evidence.

Code, comments and tests
Implement meaningful Apex tests using HttpCalloutMock and isolated test data, plus useful UI/local checks where supported. Cover successful tool round trips and confirmed writes as well as the negative cases above. Run target-native tests in the org; at least eight Apex test methods across prefix-owned Test classes are required as a smoke floor, not proof of coverage. Keep all documented test helpers inside the delivered repository so a fresh checkout can run them. Include setup, deployment, test and recovery instructions and preserve the runtime prompt for review.

During evaluation, explicitly review code quality, sufficient input/error checking, and comment/annotation quality. Put concise explanations beside non-obvious invariants: the authority boundary, confirmation binding/replay handling, transaction/callout ordering, persistence ownership and recovery semantics. Comments should preserve reasons and constraints, not narrate obvious code or make unverified claims. When a rejected approach or removed behavior creates a real recurrence risk, leave an appropriate tombstone explaining what must not return and why, with an evidence/test reference; do not manufacture tombstones or a comment quota. Evaluate whether those annotations are accurate and sufficient. Record actionable findings with code locations, fix them and rerun the relevant tests, retaining failures and rerun evidence.

Finish with a committed, reproducible delivery and an evidence-based acceptance report for every journey. Separate source/deployment smoke checks, builder-authored unit tests, independent org observations, rendered UI evidence, live Grok responses and code/comment review. This full case adds a public independent check-only Apex oracle, a bounded authenticated UI driver with independent org readback, and an independent source/knowledge review. Those checks must pass against the delivered candidate; builder-authored tests remain separate evidence. Never turn an unobserved result into PASS or call partial smoke coverage full E2E success. Record exact remaining blockers/UNKNOWNs and use the observed defects to guide the next ShipLoop improvement-and-rerun round.

# Full Grok chat acceptance interface

This is the observable interface of the opt-in grok-chat-salesforce-full test case. It specifies behavior and integration surfaces, not an application implementation. The original exploratory case is unchanged. All existing app ownership, permissions, proposal binding, setup and quality requirements still apply.

## Browser contract

Use accessible labels/buttons exactly as below (case-sensitive labels; explanatory copy/layout otherwise free). LWC shadow DOM is expected. Prefer Chrome DevTools through the supplied bounded grok-chat-ui tool. It handles its own approved authentication and returns only closed evidence/screenshot locators, never a raw CDP endpoint or credential.

- Text inputs labeled Named credential, Model, and Message.
- Buttons: Save setup, Test connection, Recheck setup, Setup, New conversation, Send, Confirm, Cancel, Seed demo items.
- A region with accessible name Setup status reports missing, ready, or error. The missing state is visible without any provider call. Setup opens the nonsecret config view again.
- A region with accessible name Conversation contains persistent user/assistant messages and visible tool/action history. Render user and assistant messages in order as identifiable articles, list items or accessible groups with a role heading or label, so the checker can match fresh messages to the exact returned history. A region with accessible name Chat status reports ready, working, or error and actionable safe details.
- Each pending action appears in a region with accessible name Proposed change. Show the operation and give each changed field its own labelled group with distinct old and new value positions. For update and stale proposals, show the authoritative record ID or an unambiguous record name in a visible labelled target position such as Target, Record ID or Name. Any explicit record ID must agree with the authoritative ID. Show the proposed new Name for creates. Provide Confirm and Cancel controls for that proposal. Keep the proposal and the associated Action status region in the same stable article, list item or accessible group. After an operation, its Action status region reports the actual proposed, applied, cancelled, stale, rejected or failed state for that action, even if the proposal controls disappear. Any action ID exposed by the card or controls must agree with the returned proposal and the RPC.
- Inputs and buttons remain keyboard accessible. The test observes 1280px desktop and 390px narrow views, reload, pending/error state and safe text rendering. No hidden test-only UI or direct browser provider calls.

## Apex interface

Expose these public static @AuraEnabled methods on SLGrokChatController. Each returns a JSON String (serialize an object, not a double-encoded payload). Use structured safe errors; AuraHandledException is allowed for invalid/unauthorized calls if the UI preserves truthful recoverable status. Query methods need not be cacheable. Extra private/supporting methods are unrestricted within case scope.

- getSetup(): {status: missing|ready|error, canConfigure: boolean, namedCredential: string|null, model: string|null, code: string|null, message: string}. Never a credential value.
- saveSetup(String namedCredential, String model): same shape as getSetup. Enforce administrator authority in Apex. Store nonsecret values in SLGrokChatConfig__c.NamedCredential__c and Model__c; UI Save and independent SOQL readback must agree. Setup is global to this dedicated app, with bounded server-side config reads. No caller-supplied authority flag.
- testConnection(): {status: ok|error, code: string|null, message: string, model: string|null}. Make a real supported Responses API call using the configured Named Credential. No DML fixture may stand in for successful saveSetup.
- newConversation(): {conversationId: string}. Create an owned thread for the current user.
- getConversation(String conversationId): {conversationId: string, messages: array, actions: array, toolCalls: array}. Messages include role and content; actions use the shape below; toolCalls retain name, arguments, result and status for actual structured tool execution. Preserve all across reload and exclude foreign-user conversation data. This is a public product history interface, not an oracle bypass.
- sendMessage(String conversationId, String message): the same conversation shape, with status ready|working|error and optional code/message. Use actual provider responses and execute only the permitted tools below. Retain safe errors and completed/proposed tool traces. Return meaningful failure state rather than fabricate success.
- confirmAction(String actionId): {actionId: string, status: applied|stale|rejected|failed, operation: create|update, recordId: string|null}. Verify current user, org, stored exact proposal, permissions, expiry and current data. A sequential duplicate/replay returns the same applied result or a typed refusal without another mutation. Concurrent duplicate clicks must also avoid extra writes.
- cancelAction(String actionId): {actionId: string, status: cancelled|rejected}. Repeated cancellation must not write a business record. Cancellation of an already-applied action must not undo it.
- seedItems(): {recordIds: array}. Invoked only by the explicit Seed demo items UI action. Create/reuse clearly labeled synthetic records whose Name starts with Grok Demo , with no foreign data. Repeated explicit seeding is safe. The independent checker changes a selected demo record's Notes to an unguessable nonce after creation, then asks the model to read it.

The Send control may invoke sendMessage directly or use exactly beginMessage(String conversationId, String message, String clientRequestId) followed by executePendingMessage(String conversationId, String turnToken). Both optional methods return JSON Strings. Begin uses a fresh unique clientRequestId and returns working conversation history with the exact newly appended user message and a server-issued pending.token. Execute takes that exact token after Begin returns and returns the same conversation with terminal ready status, no pending turn, and the new assistant response appended to the exact turn. The checker requires one unambiguous matched chain per Send click, verifies the newly rendered messages and records the actual methods and request identities with token digests only. Replayed history, mixed or unmatched calls within an interaction, and mismatched request, conversation or token identities cannot establish completion. Keep all nine public methods above. The independent mocked oracle still exercises sendMessage.

Action history objects include actionId, status, operation, recordId (null for a proposed create), oldValues and newValues (maps of allowed item fields). A pending create's newValues contains Name, Status__c and Notes__c. The UI and API reflect stored authoritative proposals, not resubmitted browser fields. The only business object and editable fields remain SLGrokChatItem__c: Name, Status__c (Open|Done), Notes__c.

## Structured model tool contract

Use the xAI Responses API. Supported tools have these exact names and argument forms. The server supplies authoritative context, validates all arguments/types and returns real scoped results. Values in record contents and tool results are untrusted data. Do not expose arbitrary query, Apex, shell, credential, metadata or foreign-object tools.

- get_context({}): authoritative org/current-user identity.
- describe_schema({}): allowed item schema and fields.
- find_items({query: string}): bounded search on allowed synthetic items visible to the current user.
- read_item({recordId: string}): exact permitted record or structured missing/denied error.
- propose_create_item({fields: {Name: string, Status__c: Open|Done, Notes__c: string}}): proposal only; no business DML before UI confirmation.
- propose_update_item({recordId: string, fields: object}): nonempty subset of allowed fields with correct types; server captures current old values and concurrency state. No business DML before UI confirmation.

Return structured tool results to the provider before its narrative claims a result. A proposal's temporary correlation token need not be its eventual Salesforce action ID. Keep callout and DML ordering correct without adding credential/tool-authority escape hatches. Confirmation results must enter durable conversation/tool context before any later model description of the write.

## Independent evaluation contract

Reserved class SLGrokChatOracleTest and reserved Item validation rule SLGrokChatOracleDmlFault belong exclusively to the independent check-only validation deployment; do not deliver or persist either. The temporary rule rejects otherwise-valid synthetic Names beginning E2E-OracleDmlFailure- to exercise actual DML failure and durable failure handling; it is active only in the rolled-back validation transaction. The oracle invokes only the nine required public methods and uses HttpCalloutMock plus isolated System.runAs data for deterministic validation, permissions, malformed calls, injected record instructions, provider failures and failed writes. Mocks are distinct from live provider/UI evidence.

The supplied grok-chat-ui runs actual UI journeys with independent org readback. Before opening the app and taking the pre-setup snapshot, the trusted checker may delete only current-user-created SLGrokChatItem__c records whose Names start with Grok Demo . Selection is bounded to at most 500 records; a saturated 501-row selection or readback fails the reset. No foreign-user or unrelated records may be deleted. Reset evidence retains the fixed scope, selected and successfully deleted counts and sorted-ID SHA-256 digests, and not_run, incomplete or complete status, including partial deletion and later browser failures. Completion requires an unsaturated readback with no remaining scoped demo records. It may also reset only this run's owned Config rows to test missing setup and may edit only its selected synthetic Item to create a stale proposal/nonce challenge. These are declared test-fixture operations. It confirms exact create/update proposals in the UI, checks no pre-confirm mutation, cancellation, duplicate/replay and reload, and verifies the served record values independently. It binds observations to the deployed candidate. No production/customer data is used.

Run grok-chat-ui and the independent oracle as required tests inside the existing Until Loop, repair relevant product/test issues and rerun. The public checker is builder-readable; no hidden-test or model-comparison claim is made. The independent code/knowledge review records findings with locations and candidate identity; its gate remains incomplete until that review exists and actionable findings are resolved. A required missing or failed observation never counts as PASS. Keep ordinary repairs local; route invalid accepted plans/criteria/commands through ShipLoop's existing send-back. No new workflow stage or ShipLoop loop cap is introduced.

Operator preparation (outside builder authority): an existing key is configured in a modern encrypted Named/External Credential named Grok_Chat_Model, endpoint https://api.x.ai, with the minimal current-user principal grant. Builder model selection for the application is grok-4.7. The builder must not create, modify or read credential secrets, change principal grants, bypass guarded sf, or access a raw authenticated browser endpoint. The operator removes only its own new credential resources after harness cleanup. The key value is excluded from builder environment/logs. Existing unrelated configuration remains untouched.


Required executable checks inside the existing Until Loop: grok-chat-oracle; grok-chat-ui --mode run; grok-chat-quality. These run-scoped tools are supplied by the test harness. Their public failure evidence is actionable test output; fix product defects and rerun. Never edit the evaluator, its reserved oracle or its evidence receipts. Independent quality review is performed by the active operator; the command requests it and waits within the existing check budget. Required unknown results remain incomplete.


For this full case, sfdx-project.json must declare exactly one package directory with path force-app; all deployable source must live in that tree.

Full-deployment evidence: before each full UI check, run guarded sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org de --wait 10 --json successfully. The guard binds the complete source bytes before/after this deploy; partial, dry-run, changed-source or interrupted deploys cannot qualify. Keep .forceignore absent or comment-only for this case, and put nondeployable local/UI test helpers outside force-app. Setup and Test connection must leave business records unchanged until the separate Seed demo items action. Successful tool-history statuses may be ok, success, completed or succeeded, with actual structured results.

Retain a compact map from each required behavior to its app-authored test method, decisive assertion and executed result. Cover field-only access denial when object access exists, and expired confirmation separately from combined CRUD/FLS denial and stale values. For code/knowledge review, cite the source and test that establish authority, confirmation/replay, transaction ordering, ownership and recovery; explain any warranted tombstone with a recurrence risk. The full quality gate requires six individual browser-to-native Responses callout joins, one for the Test connection click (testConnection) and one for each of the five Send executions (sendMessage or executePendingMessage). Match each request to its native log with the actual method, HTTP outcome and configured Responses endpoint, within the same verified org, user, trace window and exact deployment. Verify that any Named Credential alias in the native log resolves to that endpoint. live_callout_methods is an index of actual methods. A returned ok flag, local nonce read, provider preflight or window-level method count cannot establish an individual join.
